notes: Full pass: all 353 code files on both surfaces (plugin/scripts + packages/*/src) parsed into 1909 normalized-body-digest records, grouped into 35 cross-file exact-body, 29 substantive structural and 79 same-symbol-multi-file candidates = 62 clusters, each verified by one of 8 fresh-context shard agents; both documented fallback instruments were BROKEN (identity-replication-check.ts dies on a missing experiments/ script; git-lens-l-g-structural-drift.ts does not exist), so archguard (2834 entities) plus the hand-built digest index carried the inventory. NOT verified: experiments/ and packages/*/test + plugin/test files were outside the two named surfaces; the 5 digests whose 'divergence' proved to be comment-only were not re-measured with a comment-preserving comparator; no ownership/churn weighting was applied, so severity here is structural only.

rationale: 22 recursive readdirSync({withFileTypes:true}) walkers across 19 files share one skeleton (try/catch-return + Dirent loop + sorted output) and differ ONLY in the skip-set/roots/ext constants — four of the six cited pairs are byte-identical code, the other two differ only in comments.

collectShellScripts and listExecutableFiles are whole-function byte-identical copies (521b / 558b, only JSDoc wording differs) and scanSurface is a 5-member same-named family whose two largest members are byte-identical including their SCAN_ROOTS constant.

Both pairs have identical algorithms — firstArgRegion differs only in parameter ORDER (283b vs 295b), stripShellComments only in brace layout (679b vs 777b); the size gaps that made them look diverged are formatting.
diff of the two spans is empty — byte-identical module-private copies including the __unparseable sentinel on JSON.parse failure.

One comment-block-attachment heuristic in three copies (seed hit line, walk up, skip blanks, accept //|*|# lines, break on first code line); concurrency-literal already splits it into collector + predicate while the other two inline the same walk.

37 `function getArgValue` definitions confirmed by grep (plus 3 named argValue) — two forms (statement vs ternary, 97b/86b) that are behaviorally identical including the absent-key and trailing-flag cases.

flagVal IS getArgValue under a second name (86b form body-identical modulo idx->i); 6 sites are exact twins while 5 add a default value — a benign superset, but two names for one helper across 11 sites.

FOUR independent variants of the same check(name,cond,detail) harness helper across ~25 files, and two differ in success-path side effect (silent pass++ vs console.log SELFTEST PASS) — a test asserting on stdout sees different results per variant.

14 call sites of the identical 54b regex-escape body under two names (8 escapeRegExp + 2 escapeRe) plus 3 inlined copies; one outlier (fast-mode-telemetry) wraps in String(s) first — a real if trivial semantic difference.

Atomics.wait sync-sleep exists in 3 copies — two byte-identical and a third (supervisor-preempt-candidates `sleepMs`) adding an `if (ms > 0)` guard that makes ms=0 skip the call; safeTaskIdSegment is 2 byte-identical copies differing only by a private-underscore prefix.

21 parseArgs declarations: ONE shared export (gate-script-base.ts:51, adopted by 12 scripts) is bypassed by 20 local reimplementations, 10 of which share the same for-loop + throw `unknown argument:` shape (24 files carry that exact throw string).

Three parser functions duplicated across the plugin/scripts <-> packages/quay/src boundary; the flagged 796b/349b divergence of countAcCheckboxes is COMMENT-ONLY (executable code is line-for-line identical), and the copies are pinned by task-parsing-parity.test.mjs because build-plugin-dist bundles plugin/ without packages/.

Four identical 5-line ID guards differing only in the regex constant and the noun; all four already import frontmatter-store-base.ts, so the shared base exists but was not given this parameterizable helper.
Line-for-line identical guard across four stores; only the valid-status array (5/3/re-export/2 entries) and noun vary — the divergence is DATA, the logic is pure copy-paste.

One implementation triplicated/quadruplicated: get is byte-identical across three stores and write is ~50 identical lines (read-existing -> spread -> preserve unknown keys -> prevStatus -> slug filename -> withFileLock -> commit -> return get(id)) with only the owned-key list, default status and commit function name changing.

adr-store's three are thin delegates to frontmatter-store-base; quay-native bypasses the base entirely and reimplements lock/parse/serialize with real differences (<id>.md.lock vs <id>.lock, mtime/size parsedCache, YAML byte-round-trip validation) — deliberate per its module header, so not safely mergeable.
Whole-file diff after stripping line comments is EMPTY — two provider packages carry byte-identical manifest loaders kept in sync by hand, so a path/schema fix in one silently misses the other.

Statement-for-statement identical canonical serializer (sorted top-level keys, one-level nested sort, JSON.stringify) differing only in parameter name and type annotation — two copies that can drift on any future nesting change.

Byte-identical 7-line env-merge body crossing plugin/scripts -> packages, and the copy is openly declared in the goal-store doc comment (`复刻 profile-policy mergeEnv`) — drift here silently changes profile semantics for goal writes.
Bodies byte-identical apart from the identifier on the function line; ready-pool-check's own JSDoc already admits it reimplements concurrent-batch-scheduler's private helper.
Byte-for-byte identical including signature and comments (git -C <wt> log -1 --format=%ct, /^\d+$/ validation, x1000) — no third copy exists, other --format=%ct sites query different refs.

The historical six-writer atomic/non-atomic split IS consolidated (7 of 8 named writers now funnel through writeJsonAtomic), but meta-driver.ts:1356 still writes .quay/meta-driver-state.json with a bare writeFileSync and was never listed in the write-json-atomic manifest; outside that family 6 more bare writeFileSync state writers and 5 hand-rolled tmp+rename copies remain, and no test reds a NEW non-atomic writer.

One record-writer CLI skeleton copied four times, parameterized only by (script-name literal, buildXxxRecord, payload key): all four carry the byte-identical `fail` closure, the identical cannot-resolve-shared-checkout error line, and 3 of 4 identical success emits down to key names.

19 whitespace-normalized-identical lines across all three resident loops (pid-file write, stopRequested/wakeResolve/requestStop, SIGINT+SIGTERM handlers, wake-resolvable sleep, `while (!stopRequested)`, loop tail) — only the round body and one catch comment differ.

The direct-entry guard is re-emitted in four competing spellings across 201 `main` declarations: 111 files use the canonical isDirectEntry (grep-confirmed), 43 hand-roll `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1]`, 17 compare a basename-regex, and goal-store/meta-store use endsWith — so ~60 files hand-roll an abstraction that already exists.

~40 near-identical CLI preamble lines copied between two checkers (identical flag set --root/--json/--write-ratchet/--allow-growth/--reset-baseline/--no-block, identical resetBaseline guard, identical wsRoot/tasksDir/scanFiles/scanStore sequence) with --strict-subset the only delta; start-drivers' runCli is a name collision only.

Same ratchet-file reader under three names: diffing yields exactly two differing lines each — the function name and a module-local *REL constant; six scripts reference the `# baseline-count:` format, so this is one parameterizable (relPath, root) reader hand-copied per checker.

Normalized-equal bodies (same existsSync short-circuit returning {baseline:new Set(),baselineCount:null}, same /^# baseline-count:\s*(\d+)/m, same skip-blank-and-# loop) with only TS annotations and the DATA_FILE_REL constant differing.

483 of 487 bytes identical in a shared Transform-stream filter; the sole delta is `Buffer.isBuffer(chunk)` vs `Buffer.isBuffer(obj)` which is semantically identical at that point (obj is still chunk) — and both files' JSDoc already cross-reference each other.

Same 15-line parse with the same default of 1 but DIFFERENT predicate — reporter accepts Number.isFinite(n)&&n>=1 while runner requires Number.isInteger(n)&&n>=1, so --test-concurrency=1.5 yields 1.5 vs 1, directly contradicting the runner's own comment that this parse is shared 'so the runner's run() concurrency and the reporter's __GROUP__ concurrency can never disagree'.
Byte-identical 3-line frontmatter field reader and the only two copies in the repo — trivially extractable despite being small.

Real duplicate (identical SIGTERM -> bounded 200ms poll -> SIGKILL-survivors -> count-once contract; the reaper's comment says 'Same contract as orphan-session-check.ts'); note the 53b digest that flagged it was an artifact — it sliced the return-TYPE annotation out of the signature line, which is why a type-literal + function name shared a hash.

The exact try{JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync)}catch{return null} idiom occurs exactly twice byte-identically; the broader family has 12 sites but only 4 are genuine generic JSON-or-null readers (the rest are inline parses with domain-specific fallbacks).

Six independent upward walks that disagree on marker set, depth cap AND failure mode (carrier-dirs: .quay/config.yml only, unbounded, null; workflow-event-schema.mjs: 10-iteration cap, no argument, git-then-cwd fallback so it can return a git root with no .quay/ in it; repo-root.ts: three markers, MAX_DEPTH 16) — the unification test cannot see the .mjs copy, so a declared 'zero findRepoRoot survive' is asserted while two live ones remain.

Same process.kill(pid,0) probe with two different answers: server-state returns true on EPERM (correct POSIX 'exists but not ours') while driver-runtime's bare catch returns false, and driver-runtime coerces string pids via Number() where server-state requires Number.isInteger — so a pid file naming another user's process reads ALIVE on one path and DEAD on the other, and the driver path then makes a stale-pid reclaim decision on the wrong answer.

Three /proc/<pid>/stat parsers all correctly using lastIndexOf(')'); session-liveness and driver-runtime compute the SAME field 22 at the same index but with incompatible contracts (raw string, compared via String() equality, vs validated number|null), and the reaper's is a different projection ({state,ppid} fields 3/4) — idiom overlap, not interchangeability.

Not a near-clone pair (~20% of A and ~14% of B shared, one contiguous block) but the block is an unextracted ~150-line library whose two most subtle members HAVE drifted: pathCandidates/walk/TOP_LEVELS/PATH_EXT_RE are byte-identical (comments-only difference) while gitignoredPaths differs materially (spawnSync no-timeout no-stderr-suppression and loses the set on any non-zero status, vs execFileSync with timeout+backslash normalization) and the stale-path resolution kernel runs the same four guards in a DIFFERENT order with a different annotation-window test — so the two checkers give different verdicts for wrapped-prose annotations and gitignored same-stem-diff-ext candidates.

~30 of 34 non-test files hardcode the path; the writer declares only the BASENAME (path.join(stateDir,'verification-round.jsonl')) while every reader re-derives <root>/.quay/... so a writer rename REDs nothing (readers fail-open to []) and readers ignore --state-dir; the only module-level constant is DEAD (0 consumers) with a divergent ../../../ form.

No constant exists anywhere — 18 non-test files hardcode it, goal-store.ts alone constructs the same path four times, and the only 'accessor' appendGateEvent(path,...) takes a caller-supplied path so every caller re-derives it.
No constant at all — the writer and all readers hardcode path.join(shared|root,'.quay','per-task-suite-records.jsonl'), with trend-check.ts constructing the identical path twice in one file.

Core owns FULL_SUITE_STATE_REL but the two plugin WRITERS bypass it and the reader re-derives it; the highest-severity edge is the base split — full-suite-runner's --state-dir can put the file in a different .quay than every reader's <root>/.quay.

~10 files; the two constants (driver-filters plugin / observation Core) are an intentional documented cross-layer mirror because Core cannot import plugin, but slot-refill imports NEITHER and hardcodes the full path while goal-driver/driver-runtime spell it as a bare basename for carrier matching — a form divergence from the accessor value.

The gitignore/manifest concern IS single-sourced and checker-bound, but store.ts's private PERSISTENT_CACHE_FILENAME and the test's CACHE_FILENAME are two more independent spellings bound to nothing, so renaming the writer leaves the manifest pattern silently stale rather than RED.

ready-pool-check keeps a stale LOCAL sentence splitter over a CJK-aware but list-unaware regex while the shared exported splitSentences in wiring-coverage-check is list-aware and carries the abbreviation fix — so ready-pool-check never receives the fixes applied to the shared one, a real behavioural fork of same-named helpers.

Line-for-line identical loop (same heading regex, same any-depth next-heading break, same /^touches\b/i test, same {hasSection,section} contract) kept as a DECLARED mirror because packages/quay/src holds zero plugin/ imports — real duplication, but the boundary is deliberate.

Same intent but different contracts ({hasSection,globs} with DIR-106 trailing-slash ** normalization vs bare string[] dropping hasSection) — and no parsing logic is duplicated since both already delegate to the single-source touches-parser.ts, so only the wrapper shape differs.

Verified NOT a copied helper: every one of the 19 bodies is unique per-script help text (multi-line template literals naming each script's own flags) — only the name and the process.stderr.write idiom coincide, and the surrounding concern already has a shared helper (helpExit, 64 call sites).

Same name, different input domain and output vocabulary: task-schema's is LABEL-aware (directive|gap|milestone-candidate|other, order-sensitive) while ready-pool-check's is ID-PREFIX-aware (gap|dir|other) — neither is extractable into the other and both have separate test coverage.

Three same-named pairs with disjoint data models, signatures and output contracts (a 3-line generic JSON serializer vs a 53-line domain report builder; per-carrier decay lines vs orphan/live tallies; one line per mirror pair vs a multi-section aligned-column audit document) — name collision only.

Three different record schemas with three different result contracts ({ok,reason,missing[]} / {ok,why} / {ok,evaluated,reason,missingFields[]}) and disjoint field sets; only a ~3-line filter-REQUIRED_FIELDS-into-missing idiom is shared.

Reported honestly as a digest artifact, not a code collision: both bodies are the identical one-line `return parseTouchEntries(sectionText);` — parseBulletList is 44b and extractTouchesGlobs's 514b is that one line wrapped in ~430b of single-source rationale comment; there is exactly one parseTouchEntries definition repo-wide.

Same name, disjoint domains and no shared body: prod-data-audit walks git+tasks to discover carriers and builds three batch indexes (~100 lines) while red-on-omission-audit is a 16-line concatenation of three static in-file registries.

Best case in the scan and worth recording as the counterexample: driver-shared.ts IS the single accessor and both producers and tests import it; the higher raw counts came from distinct sibling artifacts whose per-driver values are deliberately SPEC-derived.
